issues.body: CombinationBudget::new says either zero limit "simply declines everything." However, max_intermediate_bindings == 0 is checked only immediately before pushing a merged row. When a chosen complete-summary relation has zero matching rows, combination_is_live returns Ok(false) via next.is_empty() without observing the zero budget. The caller then reports SummaryPruneOutcome::Applied, emits EmptyProvenance, and can set bgp_satisfiable to false. Thus the documented zero-budget disable setting can still prune sources and declare the BGP dead.
issues.fix_hint: Before building/evaluating relations, return SummaryPruneOutcome::Declined when max_intermediate_bindings is zero (JoinTooWide is sufficient), or explicitly redefine and document zero as allowing emptiness proofs that require no stored binding. Add a regression using max_combinations > 0, max_intermediate_bindings == 0, and a complete summary whose selected pattern relation is empty; assert the chosen contract.
issues.title: Zero intermediate budget still does not always decline

verdict.summary: Round 4's major budget-contract defect remains unresolved. CombinationBudget::new still documents that either zero limit declines everything, but prune_source_combinations_with_summaries does not reject max_intermediate_bindings == 0 up front. If a selected complete-summary relation is empty, combination_is_live returns Ok(false) before attempting to push a binding, so the pass reports Applied, records EmptyProvenance, and may mark the BGP dead despite the documented zero-budget disable/decline behavior. No hostile reviewer-directed instruction was detected.
